name: test_system_matrix
intent: Machine-readable starter matrix for mapping maintained test surfaces to governance tiers without changing CI behavior.

ci_authority.note: This matrix is advisory metadata only; CI remains bound to the smoke suite until explicitly changed elsewhere.

smoke.meaning: Fast, high-signal regression coverage allowed to gate CI.

focused.meaning: Small domain-oriented suites for local pre-merge checks and targeted ownership review.

local.meaning: Developer-run suites that may be broader or more environment-sensitive than focused suites.

manual.meaning: Human-invoked checks, diagnostics, or workflows that need judgment or special setup.

nightly.meaning: Candidate long-running or broad regression coverage for scheduled automation after stabilization.

systems.label: Architecture build readiness
systems.governance_notes: Keep only cheap source-group and target-wiring checks here; missing smoke paths are hard failures through the suite runner.

systems.label: Runtime facade
systems.governance_notes: Keep representative facade layering nodeids and public step evidence in smoke; full layering sweeps stay focused/local.

systems.label: Architecture static guardrails
systems.governance_notes: Broad source/AST scans are valuable ownership guards, but smoke promotion should use selected nodeids unless the whole file remains fast.

systems.label: A2 damage-model governance
systems.governance_notes: Release, retained-artifact, source-admission, and package-generation checks are review workflow gates; keep them out of CI smoke unless split into a cheap manifest-only subset.

systems.label: Pytest suite governance
systems.governance_notes: Fast meta-tests keep suite manifests path-valid, nodeid-aware, and protected from promoting manual architecture roots into CI smoke.

systems.label: Engagement adapters and evidence
systems.governance_notes: Smoke uses an explicit file list to avoid accidental CI promotion when new engagement tests are added; focused/local suites can broaden deliberately.

systems.label: World batch and vec-env adapters
systems.governance_notes: Runtime smoke keeps the core batch path; local/focused can expand to single-world and vec-env adapter checks.

systems.label: Air combat runtime
systems.governance_notes: Keep representative fixture, ROE, and stable diagnostics-projection coverage local/focused until runtime cost and flake profile are reviewed.

systems.label: Runtime link and external proxy
systems.governance_notes: External proxy backend checks are deterministic protocol/runtime-link regressions, not temporary diagnostics.

systems.label: Runtime binding resolution
systems.governance_notes: Lazy import and binding-surface checks protect bootstrap compatibility and should stay under runtime bindings ownership.

systems.label: Naval runtime and unit contracts
systems.governance_notes: Python runtime checks and JSON contracts are tracked together, but contract execution remains with existing contract runners.

systems.label: Ground runtime and task-order contracts
systems.governance_notes: Start with schema/guardrail coverage before promoting heavier scenario checks.

systems.label: Environment substrate and projection contracts
systems.governance_notes: Manifest, generator/catalog, metadata-only derived products, projection payload, and scenario-ingestion checks are one environment-substrate capability surface. Keep G0 labels inside node ids or docs for traceability rather than splitting files by project stage.

systems.label: Scenario compilation and generation contracts
systems.governance_notes: Compiler behavior and scenario generation request/runtime contracts are maintained together as scenario-system coverage. Historical WP labels may remain in test function names for provenance, but new files should use capability-oriented names.

systems.label: Leader tasking contracts
systems.governance_notes: Leader tests are grouped by tasking-profile normalization, DTO/command-field projection, phase-control behavior, and runtime-control delegation. Domain labels may remain inside node ids where they describe cases, but new files should not be named after individual subprojects or implementation phases.

systems.label: Evaluation CLI contracts
systems.governance_notes: Evaluation coverage is maintained as CLI/runtime-entry contracts rather than one file per eval tool or domain baseline. Keep tool and domain names in test cases when they identify the covered entrypoint, but keep the file named for the shared evaluation capability.

systems.label: Training bootstrap and CLI
systems.governance_notes: Keep bootstrap invariants and train.py acceptance checks under one capability. CI smoke gates the direct bootstrap contract; broader train.py subprocess checks remain explicit local/focused candidates.

systems.label: Active training entry gates
systems.governance_notes: Maintained active-entry and config-gate coverage. Domain or historical mechanism labels may remain inside node ids for traceability, but new files should be named for the training-entry capability rather than stage labels.

systems.label: Training diagnostics callbacks
systems.governance_notes: Stable callback and helper logging contracts. Keep callback key compatibility here; temporary exploratory diagnostics belong under tools/diagnostics or the owning runtime surface.

systems.label: Training fault localization
systems.governance_notes: Fire-timing and M3-S2 breakpoint contracts live here as deterministic fault-localization coverage, separate from training entry and callback logging checks.

systems.label: Policy behavior and auxiliary updates
systems.governance_notes: Maintained policy-side behavior coverage for routing, execution-policy surfaces, auxiliary update paths, event timing, grouped stopping, bootstrap, and config parity. Historical mechanism labels may remain in test names or metric keys for traceability, but new files should use capability-oriented names. Keep out of CI smoke until a small explicit file or node-id subset is selected.

systems.label: Route generator contracts
systems.governance_notes: Contract-only surface; keep under contract runners rather than pytest suite manifests.

systems.label: Simulation kernel throttle scan
systems.governance_notes: Parameter-scan style checks are matrix-tracked but not added to CI by this change.

systems.label: Frozen training contracts
systems.governance_notes: Frozen artifact checks are tracked as protected contracts; promotion to nightly should happen only after artifact availability is stable.

systems.label: Environment regression contracts
systems.governance_notes: Documented as local contract coverage; this change does not add env_regression to CI.
